known_facts_book1: Runs past Alice on the bank saying 'Oh dear! Oh dear! I shall be late!' and takes a watch out of its waistcoat-pocket.
Goes down a large rabbit-hole under the hedge, which is how Alice reaches Wonderland.
Appears in the long hall carrying a pair of white kid gloves and a large fan, muttering about the Duchess and her savage temper.
Drops the gloves and the fan and scurries away when Alice speaks to him.
Mistakes Alice for his housemaid Mary Ann and orders her home to fetch him another pair of gloves and a fan.
Has a house with a bright brass plate reading 'W. RABBIT' engraved on it.
Calls for Pat and for Bill when Alice, grown huge, fills his house.
Appears at the Queen's procession as herald, dressed in court dress, with a trumpet in one hand and a scroll of parchment in the other.
Tells Alice in a whisper that the Duchess is under sentence of execution for boxing the Queen's ears.
Blows three blasts on the trumpet at the trial and reads the accusation against the Knave of Hearts.
Interrupts the King at the trial with 'Unimportant, your Majesty means, of course.'

known_relations_book1.Alice: Mistakes her for his housemaid Mary Ann and orders her about; is frightened of her and runs from her. Not a friendship.
known_relations_book1.Duchess: Fears her savage temper — 'Oh! the Duchess, the Duchess! Oh! won't she be savage if I've kept her waiting!'
known_relations_book1.Queen: Serves the court as herald; announces the procession and reads the charge at the trial.
known_relations_book1.Mary Ann: His housemaid, named but never present on the page.
known_relations_book1.Bill: One of the servants he sends down his own chimney to deal with the giant Alice.
